_README: Literature-retrieved atmospheric abundances for benchmark exoplanets, used as PSEUDO-TRUTH (not ground truth) for Section H. Values are order-of-magnitude and MODEL-DEPENDENT (they are themselves posterior estimates from Bayesian retrievals, often with large error bars and degeneracies). 'observable' and 'domain_match' record how far each target is from THIS model's reflected-light/direct-imaging 0.2-2.0um domain: transmission/emission of hot Jupiters is a DIFFERENT observable (domain_match=far) and any agreement/disagreement is not an accuracy measurement; directly-imaged young giants (domain_match=near) are the least out-of-domain. retrieved_log10_vmr are decimal-log volume mixing ratios. params drive the offline forward model that synthesises a spectrum from the real system parameters.

targets.name: WASP-39b
targets.citation: JWST Transiting Exoplanet ERS Team 2023; Rustamkulov et al. 2023; Tsai et al. 2023 (SO2)
targets.note: First exoplanet CO2 (Nature 614,649) and photochemical SO2 (Nature 617,483) detections.

targets.name: WASP-43b
targets.citation: Bell et al. 2024 Nature Astronomy 8, 879 (JWST MIRI phase curve)
targets.note: CH4 non-detection (upper limit) is itself a benchmark: disequilibrium chemistry.

targets.name: 51 Eridani b
targets.citation: Macintosh et al. 2015 Science 350,64; Rajan et al. 2017; Whiteford et al. 2023
targets.note: Directly-imaged young Jupiter (reflected+thermal) — the LEAST out-of-domain benchmark; strong CH4.

targets.name: HR 8799 e
targets.citation: Molliere et al. 2020 A&A 640, A131 (petitRADTRANS retrieval)
targets.note: Directly-imaged; C/O ratio benchmark. CO-rich, CH4-poor (hot).
